newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golden Valley-Merukh press legal claim for Busang.
newsitem.headline: Golden Valley-Merukh press legal claim for Busang.

text.p: Australia's Golden Valley Mines NL, was still involved in a legal dispute over ownership of the Busang gold deposit in Kalimantan, Indonesia, a company official told Reuters.
"Absolutely, that's correct," Craig Ferrier, company secretary, said when asked by Reuters on Tuesday if Golden Valley was still disputing Busang's ownership.
Ferrier's comments came after wild gyrations in the value of shares in Busang's principal, Toronto-listed Bre-X Minerals Ltd, after conflicting claims on the gold content of the orebody.

Earlier on Tuesday the Australian company which tested original assay samples from Busang, Normet, said samples had been of good grade and indicated a major deposit. This contradicted weekend press reports in Canada which threw doubt over the status of samples which Normet had tested.

Golden Valley has a technical and financial agreement with the Indonesian company PT Krueng Gasui (KG), controlled by businessman Joseph Merukh. KG holds a 10-percent stake in the Muara Atan Contract of Work, which contains part of the Busang deposit.
Merukh's KG claims another 10 percent interest through PT Sungai Atan Perdana and an option for a further 20 percent of Busang.
KG's C$2 billion legal statement of claim, lodged in Canada in January, was continuing with preliminary proceedings in train and the case active, Ferrier said.

Freeport McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc, which joined Bre-X as partner in Busang 2 in January this year after dispute resolution by interests associated with the Indonesian government of President Suharto, said in March that its drilling results indicated only insignificant amounts of gold.
Bre-X had said the deposit contained an estimated 71 million ounces of gold, which would make it the most important gold discovery in a century.

The interests of Joseph Merukh dispute various ownership moves at Busang which challenge the full ownership share which Merukh originally claimed. Australia's Golden Valley is involved through the cash flow which would flow to it through its technical agreements with Merukh.
Golden Valley shares fell by one cent to 46 cents in trading on the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
